title: Stars
text:
A star is a luminous sphere of plasma held together by gravity. Stars form inside cold nebula clouds.

Nuclear fusion in the stellar core converts hydrogen into helium and releases energy as light.

Massive stars end as supernova explosions that leave a neutron star or a black hole.

The Sun is a yellow dwarf star about 4.6 billion years old.

title: Planets
text:
Planets orbit a star. Rocky planets such as Mars have thin atmospheres of carbon dioxide.

Gas giants like Jupiter have deep hydrogen atmospheres and dozens of moons.

Earth orbits the Sun at about 150 million kilometres, a distance called one astronomical unit.

Saturn has bright rings made of ice and rock.

title: Bread
text:
Bread dough needs flour, water, yeast and salt. Knead the dough until it is elastic.

Let the dough rise in a warm place; yeast ferments sugar and releases carbon dioxide gas.

Bake the loaf in a hot oven at about 220 degrees Celsius until the crust is brown.

Sourdough bread uses a wild yeast starter instead of packaged yeast.

title: Sauces
text:
A roux of butter and flour thickens sauces; whisk in milk to make bechamel.

Tomato sauce simmers garlic, basil and tomatoes with olive oil.

Hollandaise is an emulsion of egg yolk, butter and lemon juice.

Reduce stock over heat to concentrate flavour for a pan sauce.
